chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ibn Muskan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The woman should not eat from the Aqeeqa of her child, and there is no problem if she were to give to the needy neighbour, from the meat.

key_terms.عَقِيقَة: Aqeeqa: A sacrifice offered for a newborn child
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a mother eat from the meat of her child's Aqeeqa sacrifice?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distribution etiquette of Aqeeqa meat, prohibiting the mother from consuming her own child's sacrifice while permitting her to gift it to a needy neighbor. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of the mother in this specific ritual context, distinguishing her share from that of the father or other family members, and underscores the communal aspect of sharing the sacrificial meat with the less fortunate.
